q-74239.name: Question 1
q-74239.worked_solution:
A quadrilateral has $n=4$ sides. Therefore, the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral must be 

$$
\begin{aligned}{180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2) & ={180}^{∘}\cdot (4-2) \\  & ={180}^{∘}\cdot 2 \\  & ={360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's check this for the above three options:

$$
\begin{aligned}{41}^{∘}+{89}^{∘}+{100}^{∘}+{130}^{∘}={360}^{∘}\,✓ \\  &  \\ {15}^{∘}+{119}^{∘}+{82}^{∘}+{131}^{∘}={347}^{∘}\,X \\  &  \\ {21}^{∘}+{74}^{∘}+{110}^{∘}+{155}^{∘}={360}^{∘}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, only options I and III could be the angles of a quadrilateral.

q-118174.name: Question 3
q-118174.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14186732/assets/f93eab26860fffd262ce4db8927c56d77ad7710b4b7da61e190126596e968d71.png)

In the quadrilateral $ABCD$ above, determine the value of $x.$
q-118174.worked_solution:
A quadrilateral has $n=4$ sides. Therefore, the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral must be 

$$
\begin{aligned}{180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2) & ={180}^{∘}\cdot (4-2) \\  & ={180}^{∘}\cdot 2 \\  & ={360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding up the internal angles and solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A+m∠B+m∠C+m∠D & ={360}^{∘} \\ (x+{90}^{∘})+(4x-{17}^{∘})+(3x+{3}^{∘})+{60}^{∘} & ={360}^{∘} \\ 8x+{136}^{∘} & ={360}^{∘} \\ 8x & ={224}^{∘} \\ x & ={28}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

c

16∘

Correct
EXPLANATION

A quadrilateral has n=4 sides. Therefore, the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral must be 180∘⋅(n−2)=180∘⋅(4−2)=180∘⋅2=360∘.

Adding up the internal angles and solving for x, we get

m∠A+m∠B+m∠C+m∠D=360∘(x+90∘)+(4x−17∘)+(3x+3∘)+60∘=360∘8x+136∘=360∘8x=224∘x=28∘.

q-52930.name: Question 4
q-52930.worked_solution:
A pentagon has $n=5$ sides. Therefore, the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon must be 

$$
\begin{aligned}{180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2) & ={180}^{∘}\cdot (5-2) \\  & ={180}^{∘}\cdot 3 \\  & ={540}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding up the internal angles and solving for $m∠D,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A+m∠B+m∠C+m∠D+m∠E & ={540}^{∘} \\ {135}^{∘}+{90}^{∘}+{130}^{∘}+m∠D+{90}^{∘} & ={540}^{∘} \\ {445}^{∘}+m∠D & ={540}^{∘} \\ m∠D & ={95}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-4304.name: Question 6

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14186732/assets/606a6eb139d8e5813f85c608824d8313a97ddaa465b7c05c89173247550a77ee.png)

In the quadrilateral $ABCD$ shown above, determine the measure of $∠C.$
q-4304.worked_solution:
A quadrilateral has $n=4$ sides. Therefore, the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral  must be 

$$
\begin{aligned}{180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2) & ={180}^{∘}\cdot (4-2) \\  & ={180}^{∘}\cdot 2 \\  & ={360}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Adding up the internal angles and solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A+m∠B+m∠C+m∠D & ={360}^{∘} \\ (x+{30}^{∘})+{75}^{∘}+5x+(3x-{15}^{∘}) & ={360}^{∘} \\ 9x+{90}^{∘} & ={360}^{∘} \\ 9x & ={270}^{∘} \\ x & ={30}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠C & =5x \\  & =5({30}^{∘}) \\  & ={150}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-4304.html:
Question 6
?

In the quadrilateral ABCD shown above, determine the measure of ∠C.

a
205∘
b
150∘
c
170∘
d
130∘
e
135∘
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A quadrilateral has n=4 sides. Therefore, the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral must be 180∘⋅(n−2)=180∘⋅(4−2)=180∘⋅2=360∘

Adding up the internal angles and solving for x, we get

m∠A+m∠B+m∠C+m∠D=360∘(x+30∘)+75∘+5x+(3x−15∘)=360∘9x+90∘=360∘9x=270∘x=30∘.

Therefore,

m∠C=5x=5(30∘)=150∘.
q-4304.knowledge_point: Finding Unknown Quantities in Quadrilaterals and Pentagons

q-74243.name: Question 7
q-74243.problem: The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is ${360}^{∘}.$ How many sides does it have?
q-74243.worked_solution:
Remember that the sum of the interior angles of a polygon with $n$ sides is ${180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2).$

To find the number of sides in our polygon, we start by setting up the following equation:

$$
{180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2)={360}^{∘}
$$

Now, we solve for $n,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2) & ={360}^{∘} \\ n-2 & =\frac{{360}^{∘}}{{180}^{∘}} \\ n-2 & =2 \\ n & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polygon has $n=4$ sides (so it is a quadrilateral).

q-23002.name: Question 8
q-23002.problem: The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is ${2700}^{∘}.$ How many sides does it have?
q-23002.worked_solution:
Remember that the sum of the interior angles of a polygon with $n$ sides is ${180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2).$

$$

$$

Now, we solve for $n,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{180}^{∘}\cdot (n-2) & =2\,{700}^{∘} \\ n-2 & =\frac{2\,{700}^{∘}}{{180}^{∘}} \\ n-2 & =15 \\ n & =17\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polygon has $n=17$ sides.
